fixes.explanation: “You are My Son…” The writer asks which of the angels God ever told that line (Hebrews 1:5). It's asked as a question, and no angel is named as the one it was said to. Those words belong to the Son.

Priest is a fair guess, but it isn't in this verse. The writer asks which of the angels God ever told, “You are My Son…” (Hebrews 1:5). The words are about a Son and a Father. That's the line no angel is shown hearing.

Prophets came up in verse 1, so this one is tempting. But the writer asks which of the angels God ever told, “You are My Son…” (Hebrews 1:5). The word is Son, not prophet. The writer is making a point about the Son here.
Worship Him. When God brings His firstborn into the world, He says, “Let all God’s angels worship Him.” (Hebrews 1:6) ALL of them, friend. Not just a few.
Scribes are not mentioned anywhere in these verses, friend. The text says God “…has spoken to us by His Son…” (Hebrews 1:2). That's who the verse names.
Heir. The verse says God appointed His Son “…heir of all things…” (Hebrews 1:2) All things, baker. I've got one bakery and one cookie planet, so "all things" is a little over my head.

He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty. The verse says, “After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.” (Hebrews 1:3) The order matters, baker: purification first, then the sitting. I think that's a verse worth reading slowly.

A robe of gold is a fun picture, but it isn't in this verse. God “…has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.” (Hebrews 1:9) The oil of joy is what the text gives. Gold isn't mentioned here at all.

Among the angels isn't what the verse says. It says God “…has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.” (Hebrews 1:9) The oil of joy is what the text gives. And in verse 13 the writer asks which of the angels God ever told to sit at His right hand.

That's close, but it lands on the other side of the word “but.” The line says the heavens will be changed like a garment, “but You remain the same…” (Hebrews 1:12) The change belongs to them. The Son stays the same.

True. The verse says, “We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.” (Hebrews 2:1) Closer attention, so we do not drift away. That “so that” tells us why the attention matters.

Optional is what plenty of people tell their snooze button. But the verse says, “…the message spoken by angels was binding…” (Hebrews 2:2). Binding is the opposite of optional. The same verse says every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment.

Forgotten isn't the word, friend. The verse says, “…the message spoken by angels was binding…” (Hebrews 2:2). It also says every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment. Binding is the word the text gives.

Signs and wonders and miracles. The verse says it was “…affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit…” (Hebrews 2:4) That's God's own affirming. The gifts of the Holy Spirit are named right alongside the signs.

The verse says it plainly, friend. “…gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.” (Hebrews 2:4) In my bakery I'd hand out every topping to everybody, but the text says these gifts are distributed according to His will.
